title: XERO-CORE: Competitive RTS in your browser.
author: Dry-Pirate-8633
selftext:
I’ve been chipping away at this one for a while now. It’s basically StarCraft 2 style: workers, supply, teching up, with some of the C&C stuff I always liked mixed in. Power grid, build radius, walls, selling your buildings when things go bad.

Opus 5.5 did basically all of the code and the models too. It writes Blender scripts that build the buildings, and that clean up, split and rig the units so the legs walk and the turrets aim. Most of my time went into playing it, finding what felt off and getting it fixed. There was a lot that felt off lol. Gameplay was the biggest part of it, fine tuning every detail so it feels good.

There’s online ranked and casual for 1v1, 2v2 and 4 player FFA, with lobbies, friends, parties and leaderboards. There’s in-game chat too, a global one in the menu and one inside matches (team or all). You can use emoji, upvote messages and click someone’s name to pull up their profile.

Profiles have 100 levels and 46 achievements with bronze, silver and gold medals. Leveling up and earning achievements unlocks titles, frames, banners and badges for your player card, and in the locker you pick your army color, build hologram and selection ring.

The map editor goes pretty deep. You build maps out of brushes, paint materials on them, add glowing and liquid surfaces, place starts and resources, and hit play to test it right there. There’s a full guide built in (F1). When a map’s done you can put it on the Workshop, where people vote on maps, save the ones they like and play them with friends in a lobby.

Every match gets saved as a replay you can rewatch with highlights and build orders. When a match ends you get a full stats screen: economy, battle numbers, graphs of the whole match over time, and both build orders side by side.

There’s a campaign too. It’s a turn-based conquest map across four worlds and 44 territories, and you’re fighting the other three factions for it. When armies meet, you either fight the battle out in real time or auto-resolve it. Champions lead your armies, there are relics to grab and citadels to assault, and a story runs through the whole thing. It’s still early, and most territories don’t have their own maps yet.

Skirmish is there too, against a handful of different AI types. Sound is placeholder and some models are from a Unity pack I converted. I’m still swapping those out.

You can play it in the browser here, no sign-up, it just drops you in as a guest: [xerocore.pages.dev](http://xerocore.pages.dev/)

Mainly I’m looking for people to playtest it: bugs, anything that breaks the flow of a match, units or strategies that feel busted or useless, menus that are confusing or annoying to use. If something feels off, tell me and I’ll fix it. I especially want to know how the fights feel, and whether the controls are responsive or floaty.
